summary: Request: near-real-time SIEM delta stream with 30s signed checkpoints + security questionnaire evidence for Atlas Cyber audit
description:
Issue summary: Atlas Cyber (enterprise security firm) is conducting an external audit and requires a near-real-time SIEM delta feed with short-interval signed checkpoints and an evidence bundle for our security questionnaire.

Impact: Atlas requires this for a timeboxed audit window starting 2026-03-18. They will treat a mismatch or missing signed checkpoints as a potential chain-of-custody gap. The customer cannot complete audit controls without these artifacts.

Requirements requested by customer:
- A push-based delta stream (webhook or mTLS endpoint) delivering per-event JSON with millisecond timestamps and canonical UTC timezone.
- Signed checkpoint objects every 30 seconds (compact signing format with HMAC-SHA256 over ordered event batch and last-offset) to prove ordering and continuity.
- Per-tenant session affinity: events must be emitted from a single ordered shard for the tenant for the duration of the audit window.
- Field-level mapping CSV that crosswalks Redwood audit fields to Atlas schema including SSO assertion fields (assertion_id, idp_user, principal_email).
- Proof-of-redaction samples showing how PII fields are pseudonymized for GDPR scope items, plus one sample permanent-deletion attestation flow for a user_id (rfc-compliant).
- A filled security questionnaire excerpt (SOC2/ISO) with links to supporting artifacts (KMS rotation, audit retention policy, SIEM schema).

Environment: prod - us-east; customer uses our Dedicated cluster; they have provided an mTLS endpoint and Atlas SSO metadata (OIDC issuer, attribute mappings).

Attachments provided by customer: atlas-request.pdf (audit checklist), mTLS cert bundle (uploaded to ticket attachments), SSO metadata XML.
steps_to_reproduce: Customer supplied mTLS endpoint and requested push delivery - ticket created upon receipt of request
Support verified entitlement and scoped Dedicated cluster as eligible for push-based stream
SRE to validate streaming exporter can be configured for per-tenant session affinity and signed checkpoints
expected_behavior: Deliver a continuous, ordered delta feed with 30s signed checkpoints and a security-questionnaire evidence bundle before audit window 2026-03-18.
actual_behavior: N/A - request is for onboarding and evidence delivery. We need to confirm capability and sequence for artifact delivery.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 - Logged initial request and assigned to infra team (Liam).
2026-03-12 - Confirmed Dedicated cluster supports push-based exporter; current exporter emits checkpoints at 5-minute intervals by default (configurable).
2026-03-13 - Engineer note: exporter needs change to support 30s checkpoint cadence and include ordered-offset HMAC; prototype PR created (see related_github_prs).
2026-03-13 - Concern: 30s checkpointing increases signing load and may affect throughput; proposed mitigation: sign compact manifests and batch events with lightweight HMAC path.
2026-03-14 - Security reviewed SSO attribute mapping; asked customer to provide plaintext example events for three users (sanitized) to validate mapping.

comments: Priya Sharma (2026-03-12): Received Atlas audit packet and mTLS endpoint. Creating ticket to coordinate signed-delta onboarding and questionnaire artifacts.
Liam O'Connor (2026-03-12): Triage - Confirmed Dedicated entitlement. I'll spin up a test exporter config and trial 30s checkpoint cadence in staging. Marking engineer: @esanchez for signing work.

Elena Sanchez (SRE) (2026-03-13): Prototype changes live in branch. Signing uses HMAC-SHA256 with a per-tenant rotating key. Created PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-exporter/pull/214. Need security review for key rotation implications.

Security Team (2026-03-13): Reviewed signing approach; acceptable if rotation policy documented. Requesting confluence runbook update and proof that HMAC keys are stored in KMS with attested access logs.

Priya Sharma (2026-03-14): Atlas provided sample sanitized events in S3 (s3://atlas-audit-samples/2026-03-14). Requested mapping validation and a sample signed checkpoint back to them for format approval.
Atlas Cyber (customer) (2026-03-14): Confirmed they can accept compact HMAC manifests. Asked whether we can include the originating node-id and shard-id in checkpoint metadata for forensic tracing.

Liam O'Connor (2026-03-14): Answered that we can include node-id and shard-id but will pseudonymize node hostnames; offered a hashed identifier in checkpoint metadata. We will produce a sample checkpoint and the mapping CSV by 2026-03-16.
Elena Sanchez (2026-03-14): Deployed staging exporter with 30s cadence and produced sample stream to Atlas test endpoint. Logs and sample checkpoint uploaded to ticket attachments.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-14 - Work in progress: staging validation successful. Next steps: complete KMS attestation export, generate security-questionnaire bundle, and deliver production onboarding playbook. ETA for production cutover: 2026-03-17 pending legal signoff.
requested_deliverables: Push-based delta stream to Atlas mTLS endpoint with per-event millisecond timestamps and canonical UTC
Signed checkpoint objects every 30s with HMAC-SHA256 and last-offset included
Field-level mapping CSV matching Redwood audit schema to Atlas schema (including SSO assertion crosswalk)
Sample redaction and proof-of-deletion flow for one pseudonymized user_id
Filled security questionnaire excerpt with links to artifacts (KMS rotation logs, retention policy, confluence runbook)
